name: Ad Hoc and Wireless Sensor Networks

definitions.definition: Decentralised wireless network needing no pre-existing infrastructure such as routers or access points, in which every node forwards data for others and forwarding roles are set dynamically.
definitions.unitTitle: Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Continuously self-configuring, self-organising, infrastructure-less network of wirelessly connected mobile devices in which each device also acts as a router for traffic that is not its own.
definitions.unitTitle: Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Forwarding of packets through intermediate peer nodes on the way from source to destination, with every node doubling as a router instead of relying on fixed infrastructure.
definitions.unitTitle: Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Network property caused by nodes moving freely, so links frequently break and reform and path selection must keep adapting to the changing connectivity.
definitions.unitTitle: Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Limitation of wireless networks arising from limited channel capacity that all nodes share, restricting the throughput each node can achieve.
definitions.unitTitle: Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: IETF standard that lets a mobile device move between networks while keeping the same IP address, enabling Internet access for roaming nodes.
definitions.unitTitle: Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Router on a mobile device's home network that tracks the device's current location and tunnels packets to it while it is away.
definitions.unitTitle: Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Router on a visited network that keeps records of visiting mobile devices and advertises care-of addresses they can use.
definitions.unitTitle: Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Temporary IP address a mobile device uses while attached to a visited network away from its home network.
definitions.unitTitle: Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Collision-causing situation in which two nodes that cannot hear each other transmit to the same receiver at once, so no packet gets through.
definitions.unitTitle: MAC Protocols for Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Situation in which a node needlessly holds back from sending because it senses a neighbour's transmission that would not actually disrupt the intended receiver, wasting capacity.
definitions.unitTitle: MAC Protocols for Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Exchange of short control packets in which a sender asks the receiver for permission before sending data, letting nearby nodes hear the replies and synchronise their transmissions.
definitions.unitTitle: MAC Protocols for Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Contention-based wireless medium-access scheme in which each node senses the channel and waits its turn before sending, because hidden nodes cannot hear each other's signals.
definitions.unitTitle: MAC Protocols for Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Slotted medium-access protocol widely used in ad hoc networks that adds a data-sending frame and an acknowledgement to the handshake; its handshake was adopted by IEEE 802.11.
definitions.unitTitle: MAC Protocols for Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Behaviour in which a node that detects another pair's control frames refrains from transmitting for the expected duration of their upcoming exchange.
definitions.unitTitle: MAC Protocols for Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Retry scheme in which a node whose request gets no reply assumes a collision and waits for progressively longer intervals before trying again.
definitions.unitTitle: MAC Protocols for Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Medium-access approach in which nodes compete for the shared channel under distributed rules, so collisions are possible, unlike coordinated centralised scheduling.
definitions.unitTitle: MAC Protocols for Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Collision-handling approach in which a coordinating entity organises transmissions so nodes do not clash, in contrast to distributed contention for the channel.
definitions.unitTitle: MAC Protocols for Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Protocol family that keeps path tables current through periodic updates, giving ready paths at the cost of maintenance overhead and slow reaction to failures.
definitions.unitTitle: Routing Protocols for Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Protocol family that discovers a path only when needed by flooding request packets, incurring discovery latency and the risk of clogging the network.
definitions.unitTitle: Routing Protocols for Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Table-driven distance-vector scheme for mobile networks based on Bellman-Ford, whose key contribution was solving the loop problem by tagging entries with destination-originated numbers.
definitions.unitTitle: Routing Protocols for Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Counter originated by a destination and carried in table entries so newer information is preferred, equal numbers fall back to the better metric, and stale entries are deleted.
definitions.unitTitle: Routing Protocols for Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Reactive protocol for mobile wireless networks that stays silent until a path is needed, then broadcasts a search, with per-node sequence numbers keeping paths loop-free.
definitions.unitTitle: Routing Protocols for Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Broadcast message flooded through the network to search for a path to a destination, with a time-to-live limiting how far it spreads.
definitions.unitTitle: Routing Protocols for Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Message sent back by a node able to reach the destination, establishing the path to the requester; the shortest suitable path is chosen.
definitions.unitTitle: Routing Protocols for Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Reactive protocol in which each data packet carries the complete ordered list of devices it will traverse, instead of intermediate nodes holding forwarding tables.
definitions.unitTitle: Routing Protocols for Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Hybrid protocol that proactively maintains paths to nodes within k hops and reactively discovers paths to destinations beyond that neighbourhood.
definitions.unitTitle: Routing Protocols for Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Group communication in which data is addressed to a set of destinations simultaneously, either one-to-many or many-to-many.
definitions.unitTitle: Multicast Routing in Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Mesh-based multicast protocol that builds group state when a source has data and restricts forwarding to a subset of nodes, maintaining membership as expiring state.
definitions.unitTitle: Multicast Routing in Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Subset of nodes, comprising the source, receivers and intermediate routers, that relays multicast data for a group in a mesh-based scheme.
definitions.unitTitle: Multicast Routing in Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Packet flooded periodically by a source that has data for a group, carrying group and source addresses and a sequence number so receivers can install reverse-path state.
definitions.unitTitle: Multicast Routing in Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Packet returned by receivers toward the source, causing each router it crosses to mark itself as a member of the group's forwarding set.
definitions.unitTitle: Multicast Routing in Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Membership or forwarding information that expires unless refreshed, so a node can depart a group without sending any explicit control message.
definitions.unitTitle: Multicast Routing in Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Approach maintaining a forwarding mesh per group instead of a single tree, avoiding intermittent connectivity, traffic concentration and frequent reconfiguration in mobile networks.
definitions.unitTitle: Multicast Routing in Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Approach delivering group traffic along one tree structure, which in mobile wireless networks suffers intermittent connectivity, traffic concentration and frequent reconfiguration.
definitions.unitTitle: Multicast Routing in Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Sender-maintained limit on unacknowledged data in transit, preventing the link between sender and receiver from being overloaded.
definitions.unitTitle: Transport Layer, Security and QoS in Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Transport-protocol phase in which the sending limit starts small and grows by one segment per acknowledgement, roughly doubling each round trip until loss or a threshold.
definitions.unitTitle: Transport Layer, Security and QoS in Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Habit of treating unacknowledged segments as a sign of network overload, which misfires on wireless links that lose segments to poor link quality or broken connections.
definitions.unitTitle: Transport Layer, Security and QoS in Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Attack in which a malicious node floods the network with injected packets to drain relaying nodes' resources, easy where network access control is lacking.
definitions.unitTitle: Transport Layer, Security and QoS in Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Attack in which a compromised intermediate node discards or delays packets it should forward, even when authentication restricts who may send traffic.
definitions.unitTitle: Transport Layer, Security and QoS in Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Point in a network where traffic is silently discarded and the sender is never told it failed to arrive, detectable only by monitoring lost traffic.
definitions.unitTitle: Transport Layer, Security and QoS in Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Attack in which a system is subverted by creating multiple fake identities, giving one party far more influence than it should have.
definitions.unitTitle: Transport Layer, Security and QoS in Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Management of cryptographic keys in a cryptosystem across their lifecycle: generation, exchange, storage, use, destruction and replacement.
definitions.unitTitle: Transport Layer, Security and QoS in Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Continuous monitoring and assessment of node behaviour to decide which peers to rely on, made difficult in ad hoc networks by resource limits and changing topology.
definitions.unitTitle: Transport Layer, Security and QoS in Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Ability to give different priorities to applications, users or data flows, or to guarantee a minimum level of performance.
definitions.unitTitle: Transport Layer, Security and QoS in Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Variation in packet arrival times, which a receiver can absorb only by adding latency.
definitions.unitTitle: Transport Layer, Security and QoS in Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Prioritised service model in which packets are marked with a code in the IP header and routers apply per-class queueing, scaling better than per-flow reservation.
definitions.unitTitle: Transport Layer, Security and QoS in Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Time a battery-powered network stays operational, determined chiefly by node energy, its scarcest resource.
definitions.unitTitle: Energy Management in Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Practice of switching radios off when idle to extend operating time, at the cost of added latency, routing overhead and neighbour-discovery delay.
definitions.unitTitle: Energy Management in Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Powering a node from environmental sources, as an alternative or supplement to a battery.
definitions.unitTitle: Energy Management in Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Actual radio-frequency power in watts that a transmitter produces at its output, excluding antenna gain.
definitions.unitTitle: Energy Management in Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: In-network combining of similar readings from neighbouring nodes to cut redundant traffic and save energy.
definitions.unitTitle: Energy Management in Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Network of spatially dispersed, dedicated sensors that monitor physical conditions and forward the collected data to a central location.
definitions.unitTitle: Energy Management in Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Device combining a radio transceiver with antenna, a microcontroller, sensor-interface circuitry and an energy source such as a battery or harvester.
definitions.unitTitle: Energy Management in Ad Hoc Wireless Networks

definitions.definition: Gateway node with more computing, energy and communication resources than sensor nodes, forwarding their data to a server or end user.
definitions.unitTitle: Energy Management in Ad Hoc Wireless Networks
